headline: Somatostatin
punch: It decides whether GH is a pulse at all.

headline: Everyone studies the accelerator
body: So the usual story is that GHRH tells your pituitary to release growth hormone. That is true and it is exactly half of the system. There is a second hormone running the other way, and it does something considerably more interesting than just lowering your GH level. | It decides the shape of the whole thing. Whether GH arrives as pulses or as a flat line is a somatostatin decision, and given everything in the pulsatility post, shape is the variable that matters.

headline: So how is a pulse made?
body: *Somatostatin* neurons sit in the hypothalamus and suppress the GHRH neurons next door through potassium channel activation. The two populations then swing against each other in a slow cycle, each suppressing the other in turn. | GH comes out when somatostatin is in a trough and GHRH surges into that gap. That reciprocal swing is the entire reason GH arrives in pulses rather than as a steady stream, and it is why a drug that flattens the swing changes more than the average level.

headline: They control different things
body: GHRH sets how big any given pulse gets. Somatostatin sets how often pulses happen and how low the gaps fall between them. Two different properties of the same signal, controlled by two different hormones. | What this means is that raising somatostatin does not simply lower your GH. It flattens the profile, which is a different and worse problem, because from Isgaard and Bick we know the pattern is what the target tissue actually reads.
punch: ==GHRH sets the height. Somatostatin sets the rhythm.==

headline: Spoudeas tested this directly
body: They gave two GHRH stimuli 90 minutes apart to six adult males, on three different background infusions. On plain saline, the pituitary answered both stimuli without the second one being any weaker, which tells you the pituitary itself was not the limiting factor. | Infuse somatostatin underneath and the first response was blunted and the second was blunted further. Their conclusion in their own words: **the GH response to GHRH is dependent on somatostatin tone**.
punch: Same GHRH. The brake decided what came out.

headline: What it does to a pulse
body: Their specific finding is worth reading slowly. Somatostatin **attenuates the rate of GH release without changing the duration of secretion**, and appears important in **terminating** GH secretion. | So it is not behaving like a volume knob that turns everything down proportionally. It slows the rate at which hormone comes out and it ends the pulse. Switching the pulse off is its actual job, which is exactly what you would want from something that has to create a rhythm.
punch: _It is the off switch, not the volume knob._

headline: And it is selective
body: In the same experiment somatostatin also blunted TSH, which you would expect since somatostatin inhibits both. But pyridostigmine, which lowers somatostatin tone, moved GH and **had no effect on TSH at all**. | Their read was that the thyroid cells are not under the same tonic brake that the GH cells are. So this is not a general dampener sitting across your whole pituitary. The brake is held on, specifically and continuously, on growth hormone.
punch: The brake is held on GH specifically.

headline: Why is your biggest pulse at night?
body: Around **70%** of daily GH output in men comes out during early sleep, and roughly **70%** of sleep GH pulses land during slow-wave sleep. Those two numbers are the most important timing facts in this whole axis. | The reason is a GHRH surge arriving during a circadian window when somatostatin has already withdrawn. The brake comes off first, and then the accelerator goes down into the space that creates.
punch: ==Your best GH window is a brake that is already off.==

headline: One honest limit
body: You cannot sample the portal blood running between the hypothalamus and the pituitary in a living person. It is not a technical difficulty, it is not possible. | So every statement anyone makes about human somatostatin tone comes from indirect pharmacological probes rather than from measuring it. That does not make any of it wrong. It means what gets measured is a GH response under a drug that moves somatostatin, and the tone itself is inferred from that response.
punch: Nobody has ever measured it directly in you.

headline: What this sets up
body: If somatostatin gates the entire system, then anything that lowers it changes what every other input is capable of doing. That is the lever the next few posts are about, and it is the reason GHRH and GHRP both behave differently at different times of day. | It also explains why the same dose of GH does different things depending on when it lands relative to the rhythm.
punch: ==Nothing in this axis works without asking what the brake is doing.==
